tei:bibl.tei:title: אוֹי מֶה הָיָה לָנוּ
Oy Meh Haya Lanu (Oy What Has Happened to Us), by Barukh ben Shmuel of Mainz (ca. 12th c.)
tei:bibl.tei:author: Barukh ben Shmuel of Mainz
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: “Oy Meh Haya Lanu” is a ḳinah traditionally recited on the night of Tishah b’Av directly after the reading of Eikha. According to the Koren Mesorat HaRav Kinot, it is number 1 of 50. The title is the refrain of the poem, a reflective lament. This ḳinah is based on the fifth and final chapter of Eikha, taking the opening phrase of each line of the megillah as the first line of each couplet and poetically expanding the description for the second. This translation is an attempt to convey the vulgarity and horror of the paytan’s depiction of the destroyed Jerusalem in vernacular English. The ḳinah ends just as the megillah ends, with the four verses of pleas for redemption.
